title: Carbon monoxide exposure (kerosene heater, faulty stove, smoke)
summary: Carbon monoxide (CO) is a silent, odourless gas from burning kerosene, wood, charcoal, or gas in poorly ventilated rooms. It causes headache, dizziness, nausea, and confusion — and can kill quickly.
steps: Get the person — and yourself — out into fresh air immediately. Do not stop to investigate the source.
Open windows and doors as you leave to ventilate the room, but only if it does not delay leaving.
Turn off the heater, stove, or generator if it is safe and quick to do so. Otherwise leave it.
Once outside, sit the person down. Loosen tight clothing.
Check breathing. If they are unconscious or breathing badly, call emergency and start CPR if you are trained.
Call emergency help even if the person seems to recover after going outside — CO causes delayed damage to the heart and brain.
Do not re-enter the room until it has been ventilated for a long time and the source identified.
avoid: Do not light a flame to 'look around' in a room where CO is suspected.
Do not assume the person is fine just because they wake up in fresh air.
Do not use indoor heaters or stoves without a vent or chimney to the outside.
Do not run a petrol or diesel generator indoors or in a garage attached to living space.
whenToEscalate: Always — every suspected CO exposure needs medical assessment, even if the person feels better outside.
Emergency immediately for: unconsciousness, seizure, confusion, chest pain, severe headache, vomiting, or trouble breathing.
Pregnant people, infants, elderly, and anyone with heart or lung disease — extra urgent.
If several people in the same building feel unwell together — assume CO and evacuate.
specialty: Emergency department — they can measure CO in blood and provide oxygen treatment.
